 ATP Paris Day 2 Predictions Including Rafael Jodar vs Casper Ruud 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 Day 2 at ATP Paris will primarily feature a packed slate of the remaining first-round matches. However, it also has a couple of second-round contests in store, with No. 1-ranked American men’s player Ben Shelton set to be in action. As always, we at LWOT will predict every match for you, but who do you think will win?
 ATP Paris Day 2 Predictions
 Quentin Halys vs Arthur Fery
 Head-to-head: First meeting
 This matchup will feature an interesting contrast in styles: Arthur Fery is an all-court attacking player. Meanwhile, Quentin Halys, playing in front of his home fans, relies more on counterpunching and opportunistic aggression from the back of the court. Despite some solid results, Fery hasn’t been able to recreate the magic that led to his  semifinal appearance at Wimbledon earlier this season. Against a more consistent baseline player with the crowd’s support, I expect his tournament to end early.
 Prediction: Halys in 3 
 Alex Michelsen vs Jiri Lehecka
 Head-to-head: Michelsen 1-1 Lehecka
 This ATP Paris matchup between two aggressive baseliners will likely be decided by which player is more confident from the backcourt. An important factor to note is that Jiri Lehecka comes into this match after reaching the final in Basel, a tournament that ended on Sunday. That short turnaround should definitely play a part in any fatigue he experiences. Given how attacking these players are, a few key moments should decide this match, and it could go the distance. In that setting, I give the edge to the fresher player.
 Prediction: Michelsen in 3 
 Ben Shelton vs Cameron Norrie
 Head-to-head: Shelton 0-1 Norrie
 The last time these two faced off was in 2022, when Cameron Norrie, then playing at his best level, comfortably defeated a young Ben Shelton who wasn’t even competing regularly on the ATP Tour. Now, the dynamic has flipped: Shelton is a Top 5 player in the rankings, and Norrie, while still a tricky opponent, is some way removed from his best tennis. This battle between two left-handed players should come down to how well Norrie can return Shelton’s serve. The American has been in poor form recently, losing more matches than he has won since the US Open, but he should be motivated to head into Turin after a solid showing at ATP Paris.
 Prediction: Shelton in 3 
 Rafael Jodar vs Casper Ruud
 Head-to-head: Jodar 1-0 Ruud
 It has been quite a year for Rafael Jodar, who, in his very first season on tour, now finds himself in the top 10 , with a very realistic chance of making the final eight in Turin to end the season. Casper Ruud, meanwhile, has struggled with injuries this year and will look to build momentum as the season winds down. Both players had solid first-round matches, winning in straight sets, but at this point in their careers, Jodar is the player on the rise. The Spaniard has an elite return game and consistency on both wings. If he plays at the level he showed in his first-round match, he should reach the third round at ATP Paris.
 Prediction: Jodar in 2
